summary: This Wikipedia-style note is a biography of Tom Barrasso (born March 31, 1965), an American ice hockey coach and former goaltender. It covers his 18 NHL seasons across six teams, his record as the only goaltender to play in the NHL directly from high school, and his early awards and championships. It also notes his 2009 induction into the United States Hockey Hall of Fame.
one_line: Tom Barrasso is an American ice hockey coach and former NHL goaltender known for early records and two Stanley Cup wins with Pittsburgh.
key_facts: Thomas Patrick Barrasso was born on March 31, 1965.
Tom Barrasso is an American professional ice hockey coach and former player.
Tom Barrasso was a goaltender for 18 seasons in the National Hockey League.
The NHL teams he played for were the Buffalo Sabres, Pittsburgh Penguins, Ottawa Senators, Carolina Hurricanes, Toronto Maple Leafs, and St. Louis Blues.
Tom Barrasso was the only goaltender to ever play in the NHL directly from high school, without having played major junior, college, or another form of professional hockey first.
Tom Barrasso was the youngest winner of the league's Vezina Trophy for best goaltender, winning it as an 18-year-old rookie in 1984.
Tom Barrasso was the youngest goaltender to win the Calder Memorial Trophy.
The note says the Calder Memorial Trophy youth record was still held by Tom Barrasso as of the end of the 2017-18 season.
Tom Barrasso was a member of Stanley Cup championship teams with the Pittsburgh Penguins in 1991 and 1992.
Tom Barrasso was inducted into the United States Hockey Hall of Fame in 2009.
